The team completed 20 community programs across health, education, and the environment. The final report calculated an overall Social Return on Investment (SROI) of 2.64, representing an estimated Rp2.64 in social value for every Rp1 invested in the full program.

- Health and nutrition education, including balanced diets, child nutrition, and prevention awareness.
- Hands-on hygiene learning for schoolchildren, including handwashing and toothbrushing demonstrations.
- Community discussions, shared physical activities, and support for local health-education activities.
- Coastal cleanup and activities that encouraged residents to care for their environment.
- Collaboration with schools, health workers, and village stakeholders to support continued community learning.
